hint.text: Alexander the Great was a Macedonian general who was famous for creating one of the greatest empires ever.
hint.label: Alexander the Great

atoms.b: In 332 BC, Alexander the Great conquered Egypt, ending ((++Persian Nubian)) rule and marking the start of Greek reign over the country.
Unlike the Persians, Alexander embraced Egypt’s gods and traditions, gaining great ((++popularity disapproval)) among Egyptians as a ruler.
Greek rulers governed Egypt for 300 years, ((++blending ignoring)) Greek and Egyptian traditions during their rule.

instruction.text: Drag Greek and Egyptian cultural items into their correct categories.

feedback.finish: The fusion of Greek and Egyptian traditions also resulted in new gods and combined cultural symbols!

atoms.text: In 30 BC, a Roman general called Octavian defeated Cleopatra, the last Pharaoh of Egypt.

The Roman rulers in Egypt were influenced by Egyptian culture and adopted some traditions, like mummification and worship of Egyptian gods. Egypt stayed part of the Eastern Roman Empire for 600 years.

atoms.a: What was the name of the last Egyptian Pharaoh?
In which two ways were Roman rulers in Egypt influenced by Egyptian culture?

instruction.text: Match the language or writing system to the people that invented it.

text: In 1799, the Rosetta Stone was discovered in Egypt. This was a big stone with writing in all three languages. It was very useful in finally working out what hieroglyphs were saying!
